subject: Opposition to Ballot Questions 6, 7, and 8
overview: City Councilor George Scarpelli presented the All Medford campaign's case against three municipal override questions on the upcoming November ballot. He argued that the city should utilize existing free cash reserves and alternative revenue strategies rather than raising property taxes.

items.title: Question 6: Fire Station Debt Exclusion
items.summary: Scarpelli urged a no vote on the debt exclusion for a new headquarters at 120 Main Street, asserting that the proposal lacks transparency and offers an inferior product that will financially burden residents.

items.title: Question 7: Operational Override for Schools and Public Works
items.summary: Scarpelli argued against the $3.5 million operational override, maintaining that the city should draw from its free cash reserves instead of raising taxes for schools and infrastructure.

items.title: Question 8: Override for Vocational and Arts Programming
items.summary: Scarpelli questioned the scope and projected costs of the proposed educational programming override, arguing that funds would enter the general fund rather than being strictly restricted.

items.title: Financial Alternatives and Campaign Organization
items.summary: Scarpelli advocated using Medford's reported $34 million in free cash, cited Somerville's past economic growth strategies as an alternative model, and outlined campaign plans including standouts and an October 15 canvass at Hormel Stadium.
